reason: The first slice of armor-wear, wear-zero-delay-shield, landed whole at 8c55d3f: W and #wear reach do_wear.c, canwearobj() answers every armor slot, and a zero-delay shield is worn through setworn(W_ARMS), unmul('') and Shield_on(). All 22 entries below are done (9), cannot-occur (10), later (2) or no-effect-yet (1) with evidence, and missingWorkByOwner is empty. The six unported slots and the delayed nomul() arm are refused above setworn(), so no excluded branch writes state, draws randomness or prints. commitChecked names 8c55d3f; 68675c1 after it changes GOALS.json and PHASES.tsv only.

boundary.startingEvent: The hero types W, or #wear, at rhack()'s command dispatch, which js/cmd.js now admits and routes to do_wear.c dowear().
boundary.endingEvent: Shield_on() has returned and on_msg() has printed 'You are now wearing a small shield.', with the status line's AC redrawn and the game back at the next command prompt. An escaped getobj() prompt ends the boundary at ECMD_CANCEL instead, spending no turn.
boundary.validInputs: W or #wear answered with a shield's letter, or escaped. The 12 fresh cases in scripts/run-wear-armor.mjs cover a Valkyrie whose starting shield was taken off first, wizard-mode wished shields that reach Shield_on() with known still 0, and Barbarian starts whose two-handed sword or battle-axe drives canwearobj()'s bimanual refusal, chosen by u_init.c:666's rn2(100).
boundary.observables: The getobj() prompt's letter set, on_msg()'s wording, the status line's AC, the inventory window's '(being worn)' suffix and enchantment, the turn counter, and the random-number log, which must stay empty across this path: no branch inside the boundary draws.
boundary.exclusions: accessory_or_armor_on()'s armor == FALSE half, which the goal's boundary excludes so that doputon() stays unported; the six non-shield slots and the delayed nomul() arm, both refused above setworn(); the Quest helm arm; retouch_object() for an artifact; remove_worn_item() for armor in a weapon slot; and flags.verbose off, which cannot have a fresh case while getobj-prompt-leaves-the-top-line-in-c-only stands open.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: do_wear.c dowear() 2432-2452 and its whole call tree: wear_ok() 3463-3469 over equip_ok() 3402-3447, accessory_or_armor_on() 2209-2431, canwearobj() 2030-2208, already_wearing() 2011-2014, on_msg() 76-105 and Shield_on() 705-732.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: objects.h's nine SHIELD rows 653-679, read for oc_delay, which is 0 for every one of them; the ARMOR macro at 418-427, whose BITS passes uskn 1 for every armor row, which is why u_init.c:1215 marks a starting shield known; and js/cmd.js's ADMITTED_COMMANDS and the extended-command ef_funct switch, the two tables that decide whether W is reachable at all.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Every call inside dowear()'s tree was followed to a ported owner or a named refusal. The pure obj.h and mondata.h macros canwearobj() needs -- is_helmet, is_boots, is_gloves, is_cloak, is_shirt, is_suit, is_sword, WrappingAllowed, cantweararm, has_horns -- arrived as one bulk batch under AGENTS.md's pure-function rule, and objnam.c obj_is_pname() replaced the inline refusal yname() carried.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: grep -n '^export function|^export async function|^function|^async function' js/do_wear.js enumerated the file's 33 owners; git show --stat 8c55d3f listed the ten files the slice touched; npm run quality -- slice-mutants --range a2189e1..8c55d3f confirmed the Mutants trailer; and npm run checkpoint at 8c55d3f reported the suite, the seven generated-data checks and the development score together.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Two. The list is built from do_wear.c's static call tree, so a caller reaching these functions from outside that file would not appear in it; js/invent.js getobj() is the one such caller and its callback contract changed in this slice, which is why the entry below names it. And flags.verbose off is unexercised end to end, so on_msg()'s silent arm rests on a direct unit call rather than on a recorded frame.

Every recorded role is human, elf, dwarf, gnome or orc in normal form, all of which have hands and are larger than MZ_TINY, and Upolyd is false in every recorded session, so the guard is false. The line is ported rather than refused because it costs nothing to carry.

sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable from dowear() through Shield_on()'s return was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c at commit 16ff591, covering state writes and random-number order. The path draws no random number at any point, which the 12 fresh cases confirm at 30,539 recorded calls, all matching. canwearobj() was read whole because C's whole-function rule and its single *mask consumer force it to land intact, and each of its seven slot arms was classified above. Stops, partial implementations and absences are identified individually: seven UnsupportedWearError refusals, all placed above setworn() so that no excluded branch writes state, draws randomness or prints; one deliberate non-write, gw.wasinwater, with its reason at the site; one field with no JavaScript home, svc.context.takeoff.what; and one shared contract change, getobj()'s callback signature, whose reach beyond do_wear.c is recorded as a limit of this list. Two mutants survive with reasons in the commit body: js/cmd.js's state.multi < 0, which only chooses whether to clear an always-empty command queue and which seven sibling rhack() arms carry identically, and js/do_wear.js's fingers_or_gloves(false), whose two answers coincide because the arm above it has already returned for a filled glove slot -- the reason C passes FALSE at do_wear.c:2153.
